candidate_gaps.title: Production MySQL RDS holding EMPLOYEES PII has zero backups, no final snapshot, and no deletion protection — irrecoverable data-destruction / availability risk
candidate_gaps.evidence: terraform/aws/db-app.tf:18 (backup_retention_period = 0), :20 (skip_final_snapshot = true), :1-42 (no deletion_protection); ec2role grants rds:* on * at db-app.tf:210-225
candidate_gaps.attack_path: A foothold on a public web/db_app host (open SG, TM-004) reads the instance-profile creds (TM-020) which carry rds:* on *. The attacker calls rds:DeleteDBInstance / rds:ModifyDBInstance on aws_db_instance.default. Because backup_retention_period=0 there are no automated backups, skip_final_snapshot=true means no final snapshot is taken on delete, and deletion_protection is unset, so the entire EMPLOYEES PII database is permanently and irrecoverably destroyed (or held for ransom). A misconfigured 'apply' (apply_immediately=true) or an opportunistic attacker can wipe the production data store with no recovery path.
candidate_gaps.why_missed: The model rated this exact instance only for confidentiality (TM-003: public + unencrypted) and put the backup/destruction analysis solely on the Aurora clusters (TM-014). It mapped MITRE T1485 Data Destruction only to TM-014. The primary production MySQL instance's backup_retention_period=0 / skip_final_snapshot=true / missing deletion_protection is mentioned only as a one-line remediation aside under TM-003 and never scored as an availability/integrity finding, despite this being the data store with the sensitive EMPLOYEES records and being directly reachable by the rds:* wildcard role.

candidate_gaps.title: Sensitive S3 buckets (data, financials) have no versioning, no object-lock, and force_destroy=true while reachable via s3:* wildcard — ransom/destruction of customer & financial data
candidate_gaps.evidence: terraform/aws/s3.tf:1-21 data bucket (# bucket does not have versioning, force_destroy = true), :42-63 financials bucket (# bucket does not have versioning, force_destroy = true); s3:* on * granted at db-app.tf:210-225 (ec2role) and iam.tf:25-46 (excess_policy)
candidate_gaps.attack_path: An attacker who obtains the EC2 instance-profile creds (TM-020) or the committed IAM user access key (TM-008) holds s3:* on *. Against the data bucket (customer-master.xlsx) and financials bucket, which have no versioning and no object-lock, the attacker calls s3:DeleteObject / s3:PutObject to overwrite or delete the customer-master and financial records, or s3:DeleteBucket after emptying. With no versions or object-lock there is no recovery, enabling destructive ransom of the most sensitive business data.
candidate_gaps.why_missed: TM-007 (data bucket) and TM-015 (financials/operations/data_science) treat these buckets purely as confidentiality problems (public read, unencrypted at rest, missing access logs). Neither finding raises the integrity/availability angle: the absence of versioning/object-lock combined with force_destroy=true and the s3:* wildcard means the data can be irreversibly destroyed, not just read. The model's only mention of force_destroy is for flowbucket in the asset table, and Data Destruction (T1485) was mapped only to Aurora.

candidate_gaps.title: VPC Flow Log sink bucket (flowbucket) is unencrypted, unversioned, force_destroy=true and writable by the s3:* wildcard role — the network audit trail can be deleted/tampered (anti-forensics / repudiation)
candidate_gaps.evidence: terraform/aws/ec2.tf:271-288 aws_s3_bucket.flowbucket (force_destroy = true, no server_side_encryption_configuration, no versioning, no bucket policy), feeding aws_flow_log.vpcflowlogs (ec2.tf:249-268); s3:* on * at db-app.tf:210-225 and iam.tf:25-46
candidate_gaps.attack_path: VPC Flow Logs are the only network-layer audit/forensics trail (no CloudTrail/GuardDuty defined). The flowbucket is unencrypted, has no versioning/object-lock, and force_destroy=true. An attacker with the s3:* wildcard role (from the foothold in TM-020 or the leaked IAM key in TM-008) calls s3:DeleteObject across the flow-log prefix, or s3:DeleteBucket, erasing the record of their lateral movement and exfiltration — covering tracks and defeating incident response. The same access also exposes the captured traffic metadata at rest in cleartext.
candidate_gaps.why_missed: The model explicitly classified flowbucket (D6) as 'no_issue_surface' / a 'passive log sink' with no findings, and listed VPC flow logs under 'Existing Mitigations' as something that 'supports detection/forensics.' It never recognized that the forensic control itself is unencrypted, unversioned, force_destroyable, and writable/deletable by the same over-broad s3:* role flagged elsewhere — so the detection capability the model credited is trivially tamperable (STRIDE Repudiation / anti-forensics).

confirmed_gaps.title: Production MySQL RDS holding EMPLOYEES PII has zero backups, no final snapshot, and no deletion protection — irrecoverable data-destruction / availability risk
confirmed_gaps.evidence: /tmp/eval_targets/terragoat/terraform/aws/db-app.tf:18 backup_retention_period = 0; :20 skip_final_snapshot = true; :1-42 no deletion_protection (grep confirms deletion_protection appears nowhere in the repo); ec2role policy s3:*/ec2:*/rds:* on Resource '*' at db-app.tf:215-221
confirmed_gaps.why_missed: Verified in findings.json: the model scored aws_db_instance.default only under TM-003 with stride_lm I,T,D and mitre T1190/T1530 — a pure confidentiality/public-exposure framing (attack_path = 'read/modify the EMPLOYEES data'). T1485 Data Destruction is mapped ONLY to TM-014, which is scoped to the Aurora aws_rds_cluster resources in rds.tf, not to the primary MySQL store. backup_retention_period=0 / skip_final_snapshot=true / missing deletion_protection on the PII-bearing instance is reduced to a one-line remediation aside ('enable backups') under TM-003 and never scored as an availability/integrity finding, despite that instance being directly reachable by the rds:* wildcard role. Likelihood ~4 (foothold via world-open SG TM-004 + IMDS instance-profile rds:* per TM-020) x impact 5 (permanent, irrecoverable loss of the production PII database) = 20, well above the HIGH bar.

confirmed_gaps.title: Sensitive S3 buckets (data, financials) have no versioning and force_destroy=true while reachable via s3:* wildcard — ransom/destruction of customer & financial data
confirmed_gaps.evidence: /tmp/eval_targets/terragoat/terraform/aws/s3.tf:1-21 data bucket force_destroy = true (:7), '# bucket does not have versioning' (:5); :42-63 financials bucket force_destroy = true (:48), '# bucket does not have versioning' (:45); s3:* on '*' at db-app.tf:215-221 (ec2role) and iam.tf:34-41 (excess_policy)
confirmed_gaps.why_missed: Verified: TM-007 scores the data bucket as I,T (T1530) and TM-015 scores financials/operations/data_science as I,R (T1530) — both purely confidentiality (public read / unencrypted at rest / missing logs). Neither finding raises the integrity/availability destruction angle. report.md asset table only notes 'No versioning' as a retention attribute, and T1485 Data Destruction is mapped solely to Aurora (TM-014). The combination of no versioning + no object-lock + force_destroy=true + the s3:* wildcard means s3:DeleteObject/PutObject/DeleteBucket can irreversibly destroy customer-master.xlsx and the financial records, an availability/integrity path the model never scored. Likelihood ~4 (creds via TM-020 foothold or leaked key TM-008) x impact 5 (irreversible loss of the most sensitive business data) = 20.

confirmed_gaps.title: VPC Flow Log sink bucket (flowbucket) is unencrypted, unversioned, force_destroy=true and deletable by the s3:* wildcard role — the only network audit trail can be erased/tampered (anti-forensics / repudiation)
confirmed_gaps.evidence: /tmp/eval_targets/terragoat/terraform/aws/ec2.tf:271-288 aws_s3_bucket.flowbucket force_destroy = true (:273), no server_side_encryption_configuration, no versioning, no bucket policy; feeds aws_flow_log.vpcflowlogs (ec2.tf:250-269); s3:* on '*' at db-app.tf:215-221 and iam.tf:34-41. Repo grep confirms NO cloudtrail/guardduty/aws_config/securityhub anywhere, so VPC Flow Logs are the only network-layer audit trail.
confirmed_gaps.why_missed: Verified in findings.json (no_issue_surface: ['D6']) and report.md: the model explicitly classified flowbucket (D6) as no_issue_surface / a 'passive log sink' (QA Corrections Log line 1011) and listed VPC flow logs under Positive Observations (line 941) as something that 'supports detection/forensics.' It never recognized that the forensic control is itself unencrypted, unversioned, force_destroyable, and deletable by the same over-broad s3:* role flagged in TM-006/TM-008/TM-020 — so the only network audit trail is trivially tamperable (STRIDE Repudiation / anti-forensics). Likelihood ~4 (same s3:* wildcard path as the confirmed S3 finding) x impact ~3 (loss of accountability/non-repudiation on the sole network audit sink; enables track-covering for the other confirmed destruction paths) = 12, clearing the HIGH bar, and the model affirmatively miscategorized the control as a positive rather than a finding.
